utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Before we start with the housekeeping matters, I would like to make a correction on the record. In the 11th of July decision of the Chamber on the second batch of 92 bis witnesses, we admit two statements for witness - and let me just check that there are no protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As I said, in our 11th of July decision on the second batch of 92 bis witnesses, we admit two statements for witness Rataj [phoen]. The parties are hereby informed that we only admit the 16th of April, 2007 [Realtime transcript read in error "1997"] statement because the other statement is without a 92 bis attestation. So therefore this is now corrected on the record. Then I take it that the parties have received -- no, before we start with the other housekeeping matters, I would first like to deliver the reasons for the decision on the Prosecution's twelfth motion for testimony via videolink. And it is about Witness 23. On the 6th of November, 2007 the Prosecution filed a motion for hearing the testimony of Witness 23 via video-conference link from Pristina on the 12th of November, 2007. On the 7th of November, the Chamber granted the motions with reasons -- the motion with reasons to follow. The Prosecution argues that the witness has children who cannot be left home alone and that there is no one else to take care of them. The Prosecution also argues that the testimony is sufficiently important, as it relates to the alleged abduction and detention of a person named in the indictment. The Defence did not oppose the motion. The Chamber finds, in light of the circumstances of the witness's dependents and the absence of alternative carers, that the witness has good reasons to be unwilling to testify at the seat of the Tribunal. The Chamber also finds the expected testimony to be sufficiently important and the mode of delivery of the testimony to be compatible with the accuseds' right to confront the witness. The Chamber therefore finds, pursuant to Rule 81 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, that it is in the interests of justice to hear the witness via video-conference link. And this concludes the Chamber's reasons for granting the Prosecution's twelfth motion for testimony via videolink. I take it that the parties have received a short agenda, an agenda which is mainly a list of numbers with mainly MFIs organised in a way which is in accordance with witnesses. I'd like to go through that list and see whether we can resolve matters. Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. We do have it. There is -- can I add one list to -- sorry, one item to the agenda, and that is a -- a witness scheduling issue; namely, that of the Prosecution's Belgrade investigator Roel Versonnen, who was scheduled to testify -- I think it's intended but only for one specific purpose in relation to identification, in relation to a 92 quater application. Mr. Versonnen is actually in The Hague and Mr. Guy-Smith made an application to delay his testimony. I'm wondering -- he's certainly available to testify on Monday, if we make the arrangements today. It would be very short. Would it be possible for him to testify on Monday, given the state of the ruling and submissions on 92 quater application and for the Trial Chamber to hear his evidence provisionally, subject, of course, to the admission or otherwise into evidence of the 92 quater statement. Otherwise, we'll reach the situation where the case is closed and Mr. Versonnen hasn't testified. And he's one of those witnesses we can just bring with a day's -- or a day or two's notice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, the Chamber had some concerns that where it made an exception for the date where the Prosecution's case should be concluded that the exception made for the videolinks is now -- the additional time seems to be claimed more or less for other witnesses as well. Is the -- first of all, I'd like to know from the Defence whether there's any problem if Mr. Versonnen could testify -- For how long, Mr. Re?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We have nothing to ask him. It was a 92 bis statement, and the Trial Chamber's ruling was he had to testify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And the objection was Mr. -- he was here already in September and Mr. Guy-Smith --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- asked for it to be delayed and the Trial Chamber accepted his -- his application --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It was delayed. That --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was delayed. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, it was more than delayed. It was actually conditioned upon the Trial Chamber's ruling with regard to the admission of a whole series of statements and -- which is the present subject matter of a 92 quater submission. It was considered at that time to be premature to let it in. I -- I still think it's premature to let it in. And until there's been a resolution of that particular matter, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will consider the matter. We will consider the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I would make an objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll consider the matter during the first break. That's -- no travel arrangement, no passport issues, no visas. So therefore we can delay our deliberations on that for one hour. Yes. Anything else? Then I'd like to start with the long list. The first one, MFIs D89 and 90. The first question would be whether the Brahimaj Defence still tenders D89.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we do still tender those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you further explain what --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I'm not sure that I'm working from the -- the same document. I do apologise. Could you just give me one moment here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are -- we are talking about, for D89, a series of --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I was looking at the wrong document. We do not still tender those documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then D89, that number is now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was about to say "vacated," but I have not yet said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I'm helpfully reminded by Mr. Troop. D89 we do tender. It's D90 that we do not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, D89 is a bundle of documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think especially the third page of that document witness Ded Krasniqi testified that he did not provide the information as we find it there. And the Chamber wondered what -- what the value of this document is. Could you please further explain that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The -- the -- we accept that it is potentially of limited value, but there is an indication in the document that the deceased Pal Krasniqi may have been seen elsewhere at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Seen or -- seen or heard?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Heard, I believe. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I take it that you're referring to the -- to the question and answer to Ded Krasniqi in cross-examination whether another family member told him about a telephone conversation he would have had mid-August.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And so you say in this document this is corroborated, that he was heard through telephone?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: That's -- that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And do you remember -- because it's -- it's a document with several items in it. Do you happen to remember exactly where that is?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: If you could give me a moment, Your Honour, I'll come back to you on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Because I agree --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you could give me -- then at that moment I'll try to get D89 on my screen so you can guide us where to find that or just tell us. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So D89 we'll get further information as -- yes. D90, then, therefore, is not tendered any more?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Not tendered any more, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand - but, Mr. Registrar, please correct me if I'm wrong - that if a document is not tendered any more, then it will be -- the number will be vacated. If, however, admission is denied, then the status of such a document changes from F -- MFI into MNA, which stands for "marked not admitted."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D90 then is vacated, skipped from the list. We move to the next item, which is P30, which is a DNA report. If we look at the forensic agreed facts list dated the 7th of April, then it seems that the parties would have agreed on the matter which is dealt with by P30. So, therefore, if R-31 and R-35 would remain on the list of agreed facts - and that's, of course, still uncertain for the Chamber - then I think there's no need for P30 to be tendered and admitted. If, however, R-31 and R-35 do not remain on the list of agreed forensic facts, then, of course, we'd have to take a decision, because we could not expect under those circumstances the Prosecution to withdraw that document. Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But now which is the case? Will R-31 and -35 remain on the list? There's agreement on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I think so. I'm pretty sure it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's got to be signed, but I'm pretty sure it's coming.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, you will understand that for the Chamber it's -- we're not working on the basis of expectations on what will be agreed upon, but we are usually working on commitment by the parties. I now do understand that the parties, the Prosecution and Defence, all Defence teams, agree on R-31 and R-35 as an agreed forensic issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's correct. Then I take it, Mr. Re, that you apply for P30 being vacated.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, of course, subject to us -- if the agreement isn't signed, reinstating it, but yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the agreement on this will not be signed, the Prosecution is in a position to apply for reinstating the now vacated P30, which is a DNA report. Transcript pages -- relevant transcript pages are 1595 up to 1597. Then we move to the third item on the agenda, which is about D41.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I can very shortly report that matter is in hand. I indicated yesterday that the video would be reduced. It will be reduced during the course of today and a further version substituted for the existing exhibit number. And then it is tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Re, may I take it that if it's just a redaction, downsizing it to the swearing-in ceremony, that there are no objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I don't think we ever did have an -- did have an objection. I think the issue was all along the Trial Chamber was concerned about the length of it. We don't object to it, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Okay, fine. Then -- Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Would you like me to come back to D89, Your Honours? I do have the relevant pages, if it would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would let me finish D31 -- D41, and then I will come back to you immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D -- the next question now is whether the reduced video is now tendered under the same number or whether it gets another number. Mr. Registrar, this is the type of technicalities -- I think the new video, the reduced-size video, could be under D41. Is there a new Defence number attached to the video or is it the old number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The newly uploaded e-court video, which is just a portion of the long video that was uploaded earlier, is admitted as D41. And if the Prosecution has not reviewed yet whether -- of course, we wouldn't expect anything else than that just a portion of it. But if there would be any objection about it that something was added or something had become unclear or whatever, then within two days the Chamber would like to hear from the Prosecution, and then we might reconsider the decision, but it's -- so therefore it's not a provisional admission into evidence; it's admitted into evidence with a possibility to apply for reconsideration within two days. Then we go back to D89. Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, pages 3, 18, 20, and 36 all make reference to the September sighting of Pal Krasniqi in a KLA uniform in Nepolje. Those are the relevant ones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is there any objection, Mr. Re, against D89?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: This is the missing person's report of the -- have I got the right one? The OMPF missing person's report?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No, there's no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's in total 38 pages document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber will further deliberate on whether we can admit D89.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When I say there's no objection, I mean, the -- the basis is simply this: The Prosecution had intended to tender these, if necessary, in relation to the other victims. It's only on that basis. Our -- our submission on its weight would be it has almost no weight, because there's no indication of who made the statement, when it was made, the circumstances in which it was made, or anything like that. So I'm not objecting because -- on principle I don't object to these documents being tendered, but the use that can be made of them is so limited that my objection is in -- in a way a fairly meaningless one. It's a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, if the -- if the probative value of the whole of the document or parts of the document is zero, then, of course, it should not be admitted. If, however, you say it's almost zero, then, of course, we are -- of course, the -- the issue there appears to be to what extent this information can be tested. And I know that it's usually the parties that start quarreling about testing evidence. But, of course, the Chamber is also considering how reliable certain information is, how well it is sourced. The Chamber has expressed at various occasions concerns about unsourced material. The Chamber will consider it. Thank you for your clarification. Then we move on. MFI D135 being a portion of the pre-trial brief in another case before this Tribunal. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. The -- the position is that we recognise that those are Prosecution allegations. The matters were put and examined with the witness. The Defence recognised in those circumstances that the admission of the document as an exhibit is not necessary, but it had been left on the basis that the parties would seek to agree a schedule of basic facts concerning the recovery of the bodies from the Batajnica grave and their relationship to individuals within the indictment area in Meje. Perhaps in those circumstances we may simply not press the tendering of this passage of the pre-trial brief in Milutinovic but deal with the matter by way of seeking with the Prosecution a very short stipulation as to what the essential facts are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If I look at the document, of course, the probative value would, first of all, be what the Prosecution has put in another case, which might be not very relevant, or at least this Chamber does not consider that it's our task now to -- to judge upon the consistency of the points taken in different cases. If we are talking about the presence of Mr. Djordjevic at the site of the investigation, there is direct evidence for that. I think Witness 69 tells us about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There's also direct evidence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, there's more evidence. I just give one of the clear -- clear pieces of evidence which ... And then, of course, another matter is in what other activities Mr. Djordjevic may have been involved. The relevance of that is, of course, limited, if there's any relevance at all. But I think it's -- it's clear on the record now that questions have been put in this respect. It's clear that the Defence expresses its -- first of all, points at the presence of Mr. Djordjevic at that place at that time and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- wonders whether any conclusions could be drawn from the fact that Mr. Djordjevic has been accused of being involved in operations in which bodily remains were removed from one place and transported to another place far away from there --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- apparently to conceal the -- the presence of those bodies and making it impossible to further investigate all these bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. We have since this document was originally marked for identification the evidence that was adduced concerning the interview with the RDB chief Rade Markovic, which makes direct allegations against Mr. Djordjevic in person for involvement in that operation. And -- and as Your Honour rightly points out, the position so far as the Defence is concerned, is that when the Trial Chamber is evaluating all of the other evidence concerning the canal and determining what inferences are properly to be drawn, whilst we wouldn't, of course, be inviting the Trial Chamber to make findings of fact concerning Mr. Djordjevic's involvement in other cases, it is in background factual material which we say is relevant to determining what inferences are properly to be drawn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore D30 -- 135, as far as the Haradinaj Defence is concerned --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Is unnecessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- could be vacated. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, I would agree with Mr. Emmerson in that regard. I would just like a point of clarification, if -- if I could, with regard to the issue of the consistency of the positions of the parties taken in different cases. You indicated that you did not believe it was your task now, and I'm assuming that means with regard to what we're doing at this particular moment, which is a determination of what exhibits are properly in or out --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It might even go beyond that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's why -- that's why I was asking the question. It may go beyond that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: So that may well be an issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It may be an issue. I wouldn't encourage the parties to pay a lot of attention to finally seek a large debate in this case on whether or not a case is -- the Prosecution has taken a similar position. Because, of course, then the next question would be if it's inconsistent, which would be the right position. We would then have to -- consistency as such might not be an issue. We have to --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, the reason I'm asking the question is that there's a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I appreciate there's not a particularly strong body of law right now here at the Tribunal. There is a fair body of law with regard to this issue throughout the world, which is why I'm just raising the issue, because I wasn't sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And I do agree with you that there does exist such a body of law, but one should keep also in mind very much that the organisation of the prosecutorial services may play an important role there. It's a highly complex matter. If you want to raise the issue, of course, the Chamber can't stop you. The Chamber is not encouraging you to do so, and certainly not on the basis of this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Fine. I just wanted to make sure that I was clear about what the thinking was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then D135 is vacated, unless Mr. Harvey now jumps up and says that he wishes to go in a different direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I'm not jumping.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D135 is vacated. We move on to Witness 64, where we have a couple of documents. I would like to start with D159. Clothes -- a picture shows clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, it's a picture showing clothes with the identification number R-19.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Which was the focus of a certain amount of cross-examination with that witness, and so that is tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, you still want to tender it?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It is tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any objection, Mr. Re? No objection. Then D159 is admitted into evidence. Then we move on to P908, which is also a picture which is described by Witness 64. Are there objections against this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. The same is true for the other two Defence counsel. Then P908 is admitted into evidence. We move on to P909, which are meteorological data.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry, will you just give me a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. This is the short report giving the rainfall in quite many months, both in batch and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If we could pass that for -- for but a moment just so we could do some double-checking and come back it to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I'm afraid I'm in the same position. That one had slipped through our nets, and if we could come back to it later in the morning, we'll have an answer for the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's the precipitation in various places. Pec and an airport which is closer to Lake Radonjic, it seems, on the map as Pec is. We'll then keep P -- one second. P909. We'll return to that. P910.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is a picture, a page with -- I think we're talking about -- mainly about page 11 of P910, where these pictures are mentioned by Witness 64 in paragraphs 15 and 113 up to 115 of his statement. And I think the issue is mainly about the first page of -- the first picture on page 11, where the witness testified that this is not the body of Mr. Perovic shown there but the body of Milo Rajkovic. That seems to be an issue. Mr. Emmerson, you objected against this picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, we object to this collection of pictures on grounds of relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: My understanding is that it's relevant for a number of reasons, one of which is the armed conflict, to show the damage to Vujesevic Lubica's [phoen] house. The descriptions show the -- the descriptions in English tell you about the damage and also to Vujosevic Zegorka's [phoen] house, and it goes to the conflict in the relevant period, because there are -- it appears there are photographs taken in September 1998 at the time of the armed conflict. And in addition, there are the photographs of the -- all the other things there and the bodies, which it would appear, also relevant to Mr. -- Witness 64's evidence of the crime scene investigation and put his evidence in context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think, if I may say so -- I hope I'm not misunderstanding the import of Mr. Re's submission, but there's no evidence as to the circumstances in which that damage was inflicted on the properties concerned. And beyond being photographs of houses with damage to them, of which there must be hundreds of thousands, it's difficult to see how photographs of houses with damage to them in those circumstances materially assists the Trial Chamber, but it may not matter much one way or the other. And as far as the photographs of the post-mortem are concerned, there's no evidence whatsoever as to what it relates to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And there it might be relevant to know that one of the bodies shown in one of these photographs, the witness says it's not A but it's B.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, yes. But without it -- there being further evidence on -- on the subject matter, it's difficult to see how it crosses the threshold of relevance. But I'm -- and for much the same reason, it's not an objection that need take up a great deal of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: We would join the objection to the extent that there are -- that the photographs are photographs that occurred in -- in September of 1998 and the basis for their admission, according to the Prosecution, is that there was an armed conflict at that time. I don't think there is much of an argument with regard to September.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, what about the September issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, according to the description of some of them, they're photographs showing metal barricades on the road to the village of Lodza, which is in the area, on the 16th of August, 1998. There's photograph 6, images of weapons, equipment, and explosive devices found in the terrorist staff in Lodza Pec on 16th of August, 1998. They're all related to the discovery of a weapons and system of trenches and bunkers during the liberation of the terrorist centre, which, of course, is the KLA, in Serbian MUP terminology, in Lodza Pec on the 16th of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: So it really and truly goes to the period before the bodies were found.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, you're referring to no dispute about September. What about August? Mr. Re is referring to pictures taken mid-August.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm in the Chamber's hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any of the other counsel wants to say anything especially about the dates?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can I just add that it also goes to the extent of the weaponry, the arming. If you can see the photographs of -- of all the shells and the mortars and the machine-guns and the uniforms, it's -- it corroborates much of the other evidence in the case about the strength of the -- of the KLA's weaponry. And you can see photographs here of trenches and of what we would -- what we would submit is a fairly organised system of defence, which goes to the organisational level of the KLA in their conflict with the Serbian MUP and the VJ, and it goes to the organisation and the level of the intensity of the armed conflict and the organisation of both parties, if you look at the photographs of trenches with sandbags and tunnels being dug and the weaponry seized. It's all highly relevant, in our submission, for the Trial Chamber's understanding of the complexity of the KLA's organisational structure. And the photograph, I'm told by Mr. Dutertre, relates to a body found in August 1998; that is, the -- sorry, September -- discovered in September but -- sorry, but killed before. And that was the kidnapped police sergeant, Sergeant Perovic, who was -- there's been some evidence in the case, was kidnapped by the KLA on the 6th of July, 1998 in Breznjak [phoen], Pec, and found on the 16th of August, 1998 during the search. I think the evidence was from Mr. Rade Repic and Mr. Stijovic as to the disappearance of that particular Serbian police officer, both testified as to his disappearance and kidnapping by the KLA. That is opinion evidence. The Chamber is well aware of what is opinion and what is fact and usually takes already into consider that opinion is not primarily to be given by a witness of fact." Obviously the objection here is -- is as to an expression of opinion as to a matter which requires expertise; namely, the aging of vegetation based on the observation of size or diameter of tree stumps. In those circumstances, no objection to the witness describing what he saw, but there is an objection to the relevant passage in paragraph 54 and one which was raised at the time that has never been resolved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It could be at the edge of what ordinary persons establish. I mean, if you take out the -- if you leave in the size of 18 centimetres, then of course the next question is whether that witness or whether the Chamber could draw any inferences from 18 centimetres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.text: It's the -- it's the inferences that are drawn from it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, what could have been 15 years and what -- whether 18 years and 18 centimetres would match, yes or no. That's -- these are the kind of issues you're -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. At the end of it, the witness described the appearance of that section of the canal in his testimony and in his 92 ter statement as being heavily overgrown in 2002 but said in terms he wasn't in a position to say either what it was like in 1999.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

It has no impact whatsoever on the evidence the Chamber will consider. It's just a way of informing the public of those portions of the evidence which are admitted under seal but the other pages not are in need of any protection. By filing them as public documents, the evidentiary -- the technical evidentiary situation would not change in any way, and at the same time the public is informed by the Prosecution about the content of those portions of evidence admitted under seal which do not need any protection. So you are invited to make public versions and to file them, unless this technical solution would be opposed by any of the Defence counsel. Then that's how we will proceed. Therefore, where I earlier was pointing at certain pages only, it should be clear that the 92 ter statement P618 in its entirety is admitted under seal but you'll file a public version. utterances.text: Before we continue, the Chamber will give a few decisions on those exhibits that were contested. Similarly, sometimes evidence about facts is intermingled with opinion. Sometimes opinion or inferences, you would not exclude an ordinary citizen to make sometimes, however, of a different nature. Nevertheless, the Chamber is not inclined to go line by line and say, These three words are out. That, of course, might be different if it comes to the acts and the conduct of the accused, but sometimes the Chamber will just admit into evidence in full awareness that there are elements of opinion, sometimes even elements of inadmissible opinion in there. utterances.text: Then P911, if I may assume that other Defence counsel join Mr. Emmerson, is admitted into evidence. I think these were the pending MFIs. The Chamber is aware that the relevance of Mr. Versonnen's evidence is directly linked to the decision the Chamber will take on this 92 quater motion. At the same time, the Chamber does not consider it prejudicial to the Defence if Mr. Versonnen would testify and if finally the 92 quater decision would be negative for the Prosecution, it will not assist the Chamber much but it would not harm either. So therefore, Mr. Versonnen -- you can call Mr. Versonnen. But, again, within the time frame I just mentioned. Then we slowly move on on our list. I think we are at item 10, D188, Branko Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. That is an excerpt, I believe I'm correct in saying, from the transcript of a Witness K32 who testified for the Prosecution in the Milosevic trial --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- concerning the conduct of the 549th Brigade and General Delic or Colonel Delic in particular. We do not press for the admission of the portion of the transcript. The relevant passages were put to the witness in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, it's still tendered, but I take it that you do not oppose the attitude taken. I mean, Mr. Emmerson says "we do not press admission." I take it that --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We don't oppose him withdrawing his application to tender it, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Emmerson, I take it that then we'll not have to take a decision that it's not admitted but it's vacated, because it's withdrawn. D188 is vacated. We move on --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honour, would it be possible to deal with the matter Mr. Di Fazio was going to deal with? That was D64 and 65. It was simply that the weight which could be given to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If Mr. Di Fazio would like address the Chamber. Let me just have a look again what those were. Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: It's a very simple submission. It's that basically very little weight ought to be attached to -- to the -- to the documents themselves. Mr. Emmerson said this morning that the only purpose of having the documents there was to evaluate the responses of Mr. Pappas when they were put to him in cross-examination. Well, from -- from memory, Mr. Pappas was clear about his version of events. Basically they -- they concern events that took place as he and -- I think we need a redaction, if Your Honours please. Would Your Honours just give me a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: I just can't recall off the top of my head if the witness testified in open session or -- or -- or ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He was not a protected witness. MR. DI FAZIO: No. No. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But whether the relevant portion was in any way confidential is -- MR. DI FAZIO: No. I think I've been overly cautious. I'll continue. He was describing one of his trips into -- through Irzniq and the encounter with Mr. Balaj and his black jeep, and it was those events -- and he -- being forced into Glodjane with some bombing and them being kept there for a certain period of time and an encounter with the commander, and then his leaving that very day. And that's what these extracts basically concern. And from -- Mr. Emmerson put those -- these extracts that are contained in D61 [sic] and 65 to the witness and he held his story from -- he didn't -- he was unshaken in his cross-examination. I don't think that -- in any event that it's being put to the Trial Chamber that these documents go in any way to undermine his account of events. Indeed, the only purpose of having the documents there is in order to be in a position to evaluate the responses of -- of Mr. Pappas. If they assist you to evaluate the response of Mr. Pappas, all -- all well and good. But by themselves they have little weight as an account of events that happened on that day on that trip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that Mr. Emmerson will draw our attention to the usefulness of these documents when evaluating the evidence. And if he doesn't do so, then the Chamber has to deal with it itself. Thank you, Mr. Di Fazio. Then we move on to number -- no, D188 is now vacated. We have now ... Yes. D163 and D164. Mr. Emmerson, at that time you said that you'd like to have them and you would come back to the issue of -- there was something about dates, 13th or 14th --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- of September. You said these were two the same documents but with different dates. I'm a bit puzzled there because, of course, they are similar documents but not the same documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. The position is -- the position is this: D163 is a statement of Bekim Kalamashi, and D164 is a statement of Zenelj Alija. The text of the statements is identical to the text of statements that are already in evidence. And the purpose of having these statements marked for identification is because, as Your Honour will recall, there have been a number of anomalies identified in respect to the preparation of some of these documents. For example, the matter that was explored in the cross-examination of Mr. Zlatkovic which ended with a discussion about typewriting errors and so forth, as well as a number of date anomalies. And the significance of these two documents is that they are the same documents but bear a -- an altered date, both of them the same alteration but ten days apart. And since the suggestion of the Defence that the inference to be drawn from these statements taken as a whole is that far from being contemporaneously recorded interviews, they were scripts of words to be put into the mouth of detainees and forced -- so that they would be forced to sign. And I won't traverse all of the other reasons why we say that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. That's clear --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But that is -- this is to the complete the picture in respect of those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the time you requested them to be marked for identification, only you did not tender them yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question now is: Do you tender them?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is there any objection, Mr. -- Mr. Re?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, is there any objection against D163 and 164? These are MUP statements by Bekim Kalamashi and Zenelj Alija and the text shows striking similarities with other statements given by them but there are also differences.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Look, I'm in the Trial Chamber's hands. If the Trial Chamber think it assists your evaluation; if not ... I mean, I'm taking a fairly neutral view on this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D163 and 164 are admitted into evidence. We now find on the agenda Witness 69. I suggest to the parties that at this moment we do not deal with them. We might not be -- sufficiently be prepared. Mr. Guy-Smith, isn't it true that filings have been made very recently on --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- these matters? Yes, the Trial Chamber has not fully digested those. And there also might be problems as far as the rearrangement of the annexes is concerned. The Chamber, however, would invite the parties to -- you are invited to present to the Chamber in a well-organised way - and that might need some cooperation between the parties - the positions taken in relation to these annexes in their rearranged format, because otherwise we really get lost. When do the parties think they could present this? Of course, the Chamber would very much like to know exactly where objections are, where there are no objections. I think, Mr. Emmerson, you did already quite some work in that respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But I think it was only the Haradinaj Defence who presented such things and it was only after, I think, we had received that that we received additional submissions by Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I think -- I think the substance of our objections the Trial Chamber is aware of, because they were the subject of a motion filed at a time when the Prosecution exhibits were disorganised. The Prosecution then reorganised its exhibits after the witness had been brought to court. And the Trial Chamber has, I hope, a key provided by the Haradinaj Defence team which links the substantive objections in the original system of objections to the annex number, which is now part of the Prosecution's reordered exhibit list, together with - and many of them are component elements of annex 7 - the ERN numbers and the page of the -- I'm sorry, the page of the 65 ter number by which these matter can be cross-referred. So I'm not sure if there's any further assistance that we're able to offer the Trial Chamber in that regard, but if there is, it would -- it would be helpful to know what -- what specific further assistance the Trial Chamber would request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, we have received that, and it is well-organised. But, of course, it's only Haradinaj Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I -- if I might, because I think this would be of some assistance. The annex which is attached to our submission is in large measure precisely the same as the annex that was attached to the Haradinaj submission but for one difference, where there was an ERN number submitted by the Haradinaj Defence and I believe that we found that there had been an MFI number actually given to one of those ERN numbers. And that is the only difference as between the two. Our submissions are with regard to the exact same annexes and we have the exact same objections. So to the extent the Chamber can be guided with regard to what the objections are, there are no new objections that exist. We are -- we stand shoulder to shoulder with regard to the objections made as indicated in the chart that's been put forth. And I hope that is of some help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in the process of preparing a joinder with our colleagues in respect of -- of this motion. We have reviewed with care the annexes that they have provided. We will not be muddying the waters with a different form of annex. We -- we will be adopting in their entirety the arguments that have been put -- put forward by our colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So therefore Mr. Emmerson had already provided the Chamber with approximately what we were seeking. We did not find time, Mr. Guy-Smith, to digest your recent submissions -- submission, I would say, that came in, I think, only yesterday evening --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I think it came in about a few minutes before the turn of the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, that's ... And since we had other matters to discuss during our -- our early morning meeting, we just didn't find time. We'll look at it. We will inform the parties, also after having received Mr. Harvey's joinder -- we will look at the materials as they are at that moment presented to the Chamber. We'll then perhaps also give an opportunity to Mr. Re to briefly comment on them. It depends. We'll first have to look at it whether we give an additional opportunity to Mr. Re. So this is not a promise, Mr. Re. You have tendered these documents. We then have heard the objections. We'll see whether there's any need for the Chamber to -- to further seek your view on the matter. If the format in which the objections are now presented would still need -- would still be in need of -- of further explanations or additions or whatever, the Chamber would then inform the parties but in an informal way through our legal staff. And that's where we leave it for this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And if it is of some help, it's in the schedule annex 9 which has an MFI number of P1183. And we have the same ERN number -- ERN range in both documents, which is U0168335 through 8340.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we move on to number 13 of the agenda, which is about Witness 17. We have a few numbers there. The first one is the 92 ter statement of Witness 17. Let me just try to bring back into your memory that on the 14th of September the Prosecution has filed a motion requesting to admit a redacted version of the 92 ter statement. I think the redactions were a result of one of the out-of-office-hours meetings we sometimes have. Witness 17 then started to testify. The redactions, with one tiny exception, the redactions proposed by the Prosecution corresponds to what we at that time put on paper as far as instructions or guidance, if you want, the Chamber had given to the parties during that meeting. The Defence then indicated that it would like to respond to the 14th of September motion, but I think we did not have a -- did we receive a response? Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour should have received a response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, yes, on the 7th of November. Not at that time but recently.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I was dealing with history at this moment and not with this week's events. I do understand that this week, on the 7th of November, we understood that the parties have agreed to redact paragraph 73 and to de-redact paragraph 81. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That -- that is correctly understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then the Chamber would like to deal with it in the following way: That the statement is ready for admission, the statement with all the redactions proposed by the Prosecution at that time. In addition, a redaction of the following sentence in paragraph 59, which was the one exception where the Chamber gave guidance to the Prosecution which was not reflected in the 92 ter statement as submitted, the sentence being, and I quote: "I believe Din Krasniqi also had direct contact with Idriz Balaj and Faton Mehmeti." So that redaction then should be added to the ones already presented. Further, that the whole of paragraph 73 would be redacted, and that paragraph 81 would be de-redacted. That, in the view of the Chamber, is what would -- should be the result of filing, meeting, further submissions and agreement between the parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Anything to be added?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I'm not entirely sure whether the Trial Chamber intends that to have taken into account the filing as to the remaining issues in dispute. The filing that the Haradinaj team put in yesterday, which has reflected a long-standing dispute between the parties since the time that the witness testified, and it was notified to the Prosecution immediately after he testified, identifies a number of passages in the 92 ter statement in respect of which the Trial Chamber indicated in the meeting before the witness testified that the Prosecution would be required to lead oral evidence in support, and the Prosecution then did not do so. And so those passages are reflected in the motion that was filed yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I -- I think, as a matter of fact, what the Chamber said is that if no oral evidence would be led, that the evidence in the 92 ter statement in those portions would not assist the Chamber or would barely assist the Chamber. Whether we would now have to analyse exactly what questions were put to the witness, to what extent they were sufficient to give further weight to those portions of the 92 ter statement, that is a matter I will consider with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. The only reason I -- I press for consideration of the -- of the detail of the motion as it was filed yesterday is that, obviously, if the Prosecution put the witness into the witness box on the basis that those passages will achieve no probative value without clarification and explanation and then do not do so, then that is a position that the Defence assume at the end of evidence in chief and upon the basis of which the Defence plan cross-examination. And so our essential position is that if the Prosecution have chosen in those circumstances not to call evidence to support assertions that are general and which have been identified as such, then in -- in those circumstances, they ought not to -- to remain on the record. There are one or two other passages where the Prosecution did seek evidence to elicit support, but then the testimony of the witness turned out to be to the opposite effect. And I -- Your Honour may remember one matter that was the subject of discussion in the meeting, which was the receipt of some letters. And I had postulated at the meeting that without any indication of whether these were allegations of crime or traffic violations, they were of no probative value. And the Prosecution then sought to elicit evidence in support and the witness's testimony was that they contained no allegations of crimes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So it's that type of material which is considered in the motion, together with the annexes, that remain in dispute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for these further clarifications. Yes. Since the response -- the response came in yesterday and since some other matters came in yesterday as well, we'll further consider the matter. We need some time to discuss it among ourselves as well. Then we have the next item, P895, extract of a book. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That is also the subject of filings and is the subject of the written pleading that was put in to the Trial Chamber yesterday. Your Honour may remember it was an extract from a book by Maxhun Smajl.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Smajl, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The witness gave certain evidence about one very small issue, on the back of which the Prosecution seeks to introduce the whole of Mr. Smajl's book covering the relevant period in the indictment. Quite for what purpose is difficult to -- to identify, but it is objected to and resisted. And so the arguments in support are set out in paragraph 9 of the -- of the response submitted in writing yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, the Prosecution's response is the book is -- is highly relevant to the matters for determination. It's -- the excerpt is from a series of contemporaneously created diary entries. So the reliability and authenticity and credibility is given from the fact that they were spontaneously created at the relevant time during the armed conflict which is the subject of determination here. They also relate to -- they relate to the period May, June, and July 1998. The portion of which we're most concerned is the first two pages, which relates to Jablanica, which is highly relevant to Witness 17's Rule 92 ter statement and it's relevant in that it exactly corroborates what Mr. Smajl told the witness, that is, the existence of a water-filled cellar in which he saw two prisoners, one of whom was the late Skender Kuqi. Now, there are other -- there are other parts in that diary which are relevant, including the part about witness Fadil Fazliu. And the person who wrote the diary was in the position to see many of the events described in the indictment. He saw the prison at Jablanica himself. He attended the swearing-in ceremony in Barane on the 20th of July, 1998. His descriptions of those events is relevant to assessing the veracity of the hearsay information appearing in Witness 17's Rule 92 ter statement and in his testimony and the entire excerpt provides the context which the Trial Chamber needs to assess the credibility of the person writing the diary and the veracity of what's contained in it. So in our submission, you've got to look at the entire document in its context to see how it relates to the events, the subject of the indictment and to provide some very relevant, valuable and incriminating evidence which is corroborated throughout -- has been corroborated throughout the trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I don't wish, if I may, to repeat that the arguments that are set out in writing. We would simply refer the Trial Chamber to paragraph 9 of the -- of the written submission. This is not a contemporaneous diary. It's a subsequently written account by this individual of recollections. It is plainly hearsay. It plainly goes to the acts and conducts, in certain passages, of the accused. It is material in which no weight, in our submission, could properly attach. And if the Prosecution thought Mr. Smajl had relevant evidence to give, they would have no doubt have called him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. I would refer the Chamber to our paragraphs, I believe, 29 -- 29 through 33 of our filing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I also rely on the matters set forth in the filing that Mr. Guy-Smith just referred to. In addition to which, it is totally misleading, and I don't -- I'm sure that Mr. Re hasn't said it deliberately. Obviously, he hasn't read carefully enough the passage from the book. There is absolutely no suggestion that this Mr. Smajl saw Skender Kuqi in the water-filled cellar. It is not borne out at all by that. Mr. -- this book does -- is not corroborated by the Witness 17's observations. In fact, Witness 17 said that he did go to the barracks but he did not examine any of these locations. The document is described as relating to Smajl's threat of liquidation by Lahi Brahimi. I quote the document description that appears in the exhibit list. There is no threat ever found in that book. And whatever basis for it seems to have emerged purely from the fantasy of Witness 17. It's simply not contained there. All in all, this is a witness who should have been produced so that the Trial Chamber could assess whether anything that he had written in his book was of any validity at all. But it simply cannot be corroborated by Witness 17. So I -- I object to the admission of the book in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I -- I correct where I said it's -- it's clear he said he saw Skender Kuqi. What he actually said was he -- he -- "They told me to squat and look into the cellar, which I did. Sitting down I saw two people in the corner standing in the water. It was a distressing sight, even though I did not know who those people were." He then goes on to say that "Skender Kuqi and a man from Polac, Nugat Sati [phoen] had experienced the same fate," et cetera. "Had been subject to torture, and ended up in the water-filled cellar." That's the connection. The connection is he saw people in that prison in the water himself and he also was aware that Skender Kuqi had suffered the same fate and that's corroborated by the evidence of witnesses who saw Skender Kuqi in that cellar in the same time period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is the awareness sourced in any way?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes. It's the -- it's the -- it's the effect of many people knowing about it. Some people seeing it, other people describing it to people, and it being reported. It's almost becoming an instance of common knowledge in the area that Skender Kuqi met that fate and this fellow, Smajl, saw people suffering the same fate in the cellar as that which Mr. Skender Kuqi met. So it has corroborative value.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd be very grateful if Mr. Re could refer us to one point in the evidence that has so far been received by this Tribunal of Skender Kuqi ever having been seen in a water-filled cellar. There is no such evidence before the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, this seems to be an invitation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Jablanica. In the prison where this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the prison, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- where the water-filled cellar was and the same area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber will rule on the matter right away. The 92 ter statement in paragraphs 68 and 69 deal with the book. The witness there describes discussions he had with the author of the book. The 92 ter statement is -- in this respect seems to be the better evidence. And if the Prosecution would like to have parts of the book admitted into evidence which are not covered by the testimony of the 92 ter statement, then you would have to identify those portions precisely, Mr. Re, and explain why they are relevant and of probative value. So therefore, P895 now gets the status of marked, not admitted. But if there are any specific portions, Mr. Re, you know that you could address the Chamber on that. We now move to P896, P897, P898, and P902. These are all documents produced by a witness who did not yet appear before this Chamber. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, exactly so. And they are addressed in paragraph 10 in writing of the motion that we filed yesterday. We would respectfully submit that these are, as you say, documents purportedly produced but not identified by a witness whose name I won't refer to in open session but who is the subject of an unfulfilled subpoena application and, I believe, at least consideration of contempt proceedings. The witness statement from that witness contradicts the content of these documents in a number of respects, and the Trial Chamber may remember that I cross-examined Witness 17 about a passage from the witness statement of the witness concerned in relation to his investigation into the death of Sanije Balaj, which contained an account utterly at variance with the accounts recorded in the exhibits that the Trial Chamber has just identified. And we respectfully submit that unless or until that witness is called to testify, these documents should not be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, is there anything you'd like to add? If not, then the Chamber will consider the matter during the next break.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There's nothing I can add at the moment. Could I just ask that this matter be deferred today, consideration of this be conferred -- what's the word I used? Deferred.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll include that in our considerations.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then P906 is a pseudonym sheet in relation to Witness 17 which is admitted into evidence in the absence of any response to what I just said. Then D156, D157, and D158, Mr. Re, are military documents and the Chamber would like to know whether you have any objections against admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: These are the Rrustem Tetaj ones, I think, aren't they? They have his name on them. Sorry, Rrustem Berisha.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. They --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I can assist to this extent. The Trial Chamber will find reference to this in paragraph 11 of the written motion filed yesterday. These were documents that were provided by Witness 17 to the Prosecution in electronic form and upon which he was cross-examined. They are contemporary orders, some of which bear the name of the person for who he was --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I don't object. There's no objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objection against either of the three. Yes. Then D156, D157, and D158 are admitted into evidence. Then we move on. We now come to Witness 56.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think, if I may say something -- just before Your Honour moves on, I think there is an additional document under item 13.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, yes, I think -- no, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just check. I must have missed something.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I remind the Trial Chamber of what this is? It's on the list that was provided by --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I've seen that. I'm just trying to find my notes on this matter at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I -- can I assist to this extent. There's a -- there's a technical problem in relation to this document, because the e-court system - and I think the registrar may be able to confirm this - finds nothing under D161.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D161, could we ask Mr. Registrar whether this item is known to him and which party tendered that. If he can't identify it, D161 will be identified as the mysterious guest in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I can identify it whenever --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- the moment is convenient. D161 should have been Defence document 1D56-0019, and it was the subject of cross-examination of Witness 17 at transcript page 7747. And just to remind the Trial Chamber, it was a -- a document again relating to the appointment on the 20th of August of a new general -- a new staff in the Dukagjin area under the command of Tahir Zemaj. And the significance of the document was that it was in all respects identical to a document that had been produced by Witness 17 except that Witness 17 was not on it as the Chief of Staff. In other words, in the document he produced of that date, he was named as Chief of Staff. But in the document which is 1D61, 1D56-0019, which was in the cross-examination bundle, somebody else was named as Chief of Staff. So that is the document that it relates to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is it uploaded in the e-court system? Because that seems to be a problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, there's obviously been a technical error in uploading it. Yes, it is -- it is uploaded it into e-court, but -- well, no -- but it hasn't been linked within the system.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, we'll -- First of all, Mr. Re, are you familiar with the document? D161. Although it doesn't appear in e-court. Mr. Guy-Smith, if you can assist us.
