The Chamber will not draw any consequences out of this non-admission for the admission of the 92 ter statement. Then we move on to item 22 on the agenda. We're talking about D162 and P919 and P920. They have been MFI'd. They have, however, not been tendered. Mr. Emmerson, D162.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, D162 is tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is tendered. Any objections against D162? Not. Therefore, admitted into evidence. We now move to P919 and P920, the first one being a criminal report against an unknown perpetrator, Popadic and Jovanovic as victims. P920, it is a document from the Serbian Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are they tendered?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They are tendered. Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then assuming that other Defence counsel join --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Absolutely not. No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I was a bit -- you said "absolutely not." And I was assuming that you would join. And, as a matter of fact, you absolutely wanted to join.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's now clear --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: What I meant was absolutely not, meaning no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. P919 and P920 are admitted into evidence. We now move on to the documents tendered through Witness 8. May I remind the parties that the Chamber earlier considered in relation to Witness 8 that if at a later stage the Chamber were to receive evidence from other sources that would shed a different light on the reliability and credibility of Witness 8 as now perceived by the Chamber, that it would then remain open to the Chamber to reconsider proprio motu or on the motion of one of the parties whether Witness 8 should be called to complete his testimony. The Chamber has not received any evidence nor any submission by the parties which would lead it to reconsider its position. Therefore, under those circumstances, the Chamber denies admission of all outstanding exhibits tendered through this witness, which are D93 to D95, D97 through D105, and P40. I think that the pseudonym sheet was already admitted. We'll verify that. But that would be not an outstanding exhibit any more, so that is not covered by this ruling. This ruling only deals with outstanding exhibits. Then we move on to Witness 17, 24 on the agenda. P906 is a pseudonym sheet for Witness 17. In the absence of any objections, should be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My attention was drawn to the fact that for the second time today I admitted the pseudonym sheet of Witness 17. So the parties can be assured that there could be no doubt as to its admission. For Witness 55, there's also P915, pseudonym sheet. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We would respectfully invite the Trial Chamber to consider deferring the question of the admission of that pseudonym sheet until the Trial Chamber has decided what to do in respect of the presence on the record of the testimony given by that witness in chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, of course we -- we might -- if we are just talking about the pseudonym sheet, I think it's the only document that identifies the person that appeared before the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore whatever reason you would give for any subsequent -- any -- any --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- any sequential decisions --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I take Your Honour's point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's good to know in respect of whom -- if, for example, if you would ever order any medical examination of a person, then you would at least have to know who that person is. So therefore, I'm inclined - and my colleagues also are inclined - not to defer that but to admit P915 into evidence. The next item on the agenda, in relation to Witness 71, a video taken at Hotel Pastrik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. This video tendered through Witness 71 is a video which was MFI'd but not tendered, Mr. -- Mr. Re. Do you want to tender it?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I -- I oppose simply on the basis it is of nil probative value. The witness testified and gave unchallenged evidence that he attended Hotel Pastrik and that he was unable to identify the remains of his brother. So there's no challenge to the issue of his presence there. Insofar as it is the words spoken on the videotape which the Prosecution seek to rely upon, as the Trial Chamber observed during the course of the testimony, the passage is incomprehensible and consists of a number of leading propositions being put to the witness which were then not in any way supported or reflected in his testimony. So it adds nothing to the probative weight of the witness's evidence. There is no dispute to the fact that he was present at Hotel Pastrik. And beyond that neither the video nor the transcript can have any probative value in the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's incorrect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First of all, where I earlier said that it was tendered but not -- no admission was sought, I think this video was played twice; once in relation to Witness 71 and once in -- I think it was Witness Gojkovic who was shown this video as well. Could you please respond.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's in evidence. The video is in evidence. I can't tell you the exhibit number. It's an extract --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's an extract of the video which is already in evidence and it's an extract which we had enhanced so that you can hear the witness's -- what the witness is saying. The value of it is it's the witness's contemporaneous account of what happened to his relative when he went to identify his relative. The words are audible. There is a transcript. It's on the -- it's been digitised. You can see it. And it's already in evidence. It's just an extract which has been enhanced. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It -- I just can't see how the Defence can object to an extract of a video being separately tendered with an enhancement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But at that time apparently with no audible text on the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That -- that may have been the case. But the -- as I understand it, the enhanced video has been disclosed and, I'm told, uploaded into e-court as the correct -- I'm told as the authentic or -- as the authentic version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I think one of the arguments was that it doesn't add anything. Is -- is there any dispute, Mr. Emmerson, that the -- what was said by the witness at that time about what had happened, that -- that that's in any way inconsistent with what he says now?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm not sure I fully understand Your Honour's question. The --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if we -- Mr. Re says it's the contemporaneous version of what he told at the time. Therefore, of course, if that adds anything --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But as Your Honour will recall, the passage is completely incomprehensible and it is spoken by a man who says he doesn't speak fluent Serbian or understand it. And I don't know if Your Honour recalls the passage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't remember the -- I remember the images, but I don't remember the exact text.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, in fact Your Honour -- Your Honour observed in relation to the transcript during the course of the testimony of Witness 71 that it was frankly impossible to determine what he was saying. It's snippets of conversation. And then there are suggestions put by other people who are referred to on the transcript as "police officers." And there is no coherent material in the transcript at all. On the other hand, the witness has given oral evidence before the Trial Chamber and such testimony as he's given is direct testimony. There's not -- there's not a question of consistency or inconsistency. The transcript is simply incomprehensible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You would say being incomprehensible, it could not possibly add anything to --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It could not possibly add anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, you --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The issue is, as I recall -- I'd have to go back and look at this -- is that the witness is now older. It was nine years ago. His Serbian then was better than his Serbian now. He was speaking to -- and I think it was Professor Dunjic, I think you can see in the frame - I'm going from memory - sorry, it was Judge Gojkovic. You could see him -- could see them talking and he was telling the judge what he'd heard about what happened to his brother. Now, that was evidence which - I'm going by memory - I don't think he was able to reproduce in court, but it's the best-available evidence of what he said at the time in going to look for his -- his relative. Now, there is a transcript, and it is digitised. I'm told it's part of Exhibit P452, for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson -- Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The witness was not speaking Serbian. He was speaking through a translator. It's very clear when you look at the film that that's part of what's going on. And, second of all, he indicated that at that time back then, his Serbian was poor at best. I just wanted to deal with those particular factual issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Those are matters which obviously are relevant. But critically the transcript is incomprehensible. There is no account recorded by the witness in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There's a transcript at P01192, which is the enhanced -- the transcript of the enhanced tape. The whole -- the whole purpose of the excerpt was to enhance it to -- the Dutch -- the Dutch forensic laboratories went and enhanced it to a quality where it could be heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And it has been transcribed. The Defence does have a -- a transcript of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If they go away and listen to it, I'm sure we can resolve this.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Re is misunderstanding me. We all had the enhanced transcript available to us in court. The enhanced transcript produces an incomprehensible conversation not because you can't hear it, but because even assuming the enhancement is correct there's snippets of snatched words where police officers are putting propositions to the witness. There is no response recorded to the propositions and no account given. It's completely incomprehensible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, could -- could you guide the Chamber as to where exactly in this document to find what you consider to be a understandable ... I have got it in front of me. So if you take me to the pages where we find that, we can decide. It's a five-page document. I'm now on page 3. I have not found yet what you said the exhibit would bring us.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. I've got it here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I've got a printout. At first -- I mean, the question of comprehensibility is a side issue, in my submission. It's the issue of what the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, you said it is relevant because it gives a contemporaneous report to others on the disappearance of a family member of Witness 71. So I'm inviting you now to tell us where we find a understandable ...

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. It starts where he's -- where he's looking at the body.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you -- if you give me the --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Page 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- page of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Page 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. I'm on page 1 of the transcript now, yes. It started where there is a wedding --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If you just give me a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's speaker 2. Speaker 2 is -- is the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: They're asking about a wedding band. "No, there isn't."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Then they -- hang on. Where is it? I'm -- I'm sorry. I'm going to have to return to this, if the Trial Chamber would allow me to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Mr. Re, if you tell us what we find there and if we invite you to show where it is, and you say well -- no, that means that you're not properly prepared.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honour, there are over 100 documents on the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. What do you think I did yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: On this particular one I need to look at it again. All the others I think I've been okay so far. Just on this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then take care, because we want to -- well, we'll move on. We might decide to read it and to decide on the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could I just remind the Trial Chamber --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- where the matter came up in evidence and the Trial Chamber's reaction to it at that stage. Which is 10037, lines 1 to 15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber at this moment decides that the video tendered under P1192 is not admitted into evidence. And if the Prosecution wants the Chamber to reconsider this decision, then an application should be made. The Chamber is not encouraging, also on the basis of its own recollection, apart from now looking at the transcript but also recollection of what we thought at the time, is not encouraging the Prosecution to do so. Then we move on to 27, MFIs D123 up to and including D129.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I just indicate --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, I think you requested to be heard before we would decide on the admission of these Defence exhibits. And that was on the 31st of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: These documents are, in my submission, in the same general category as the ones I've referred to before, contemporaneous reports, statements, and on that basis, we don't object to the -- the Trial Chamber receiving them into evidence. The -- the amount of weight you can give them must be considered in light of all -- all of the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's the only basis upon which we don't object to the admission into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And, of course, you'll expect equal treatment, isn't it, for Prosecution exhibits?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, I think it goes without saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then D123 up to and including D129 are admitted into evidence. The next item on the agenda is 28.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just -- just before Your Honour moves on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just to be clear, D124 we believe to be also exhibited as P871.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll check that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Or at least marked for identification, I'm sorry, as P871.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if it's marked for identification only, we should come across it, because we're dealing with all MFIs.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But I make a note that D124 you think is the same as P871.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And D126 is the same as P395.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If they are the same documents, if they are admitted into evidence, then the Chamber will accordingly vacate the numbers, if the documents are really exactly the same. We move on to item 28 on the agenda. I think all of the exhibits have been dealt with, so there's no item left as far as the Zyrapi exhibits are concerned. I move on to 29, Witness 28. We have the numbers 195 -- Defence 195. And I start with 195 up to 202, weekly reports of human rights organisations in Kosovo; number 203 being used by Mr. Harvey in cross-examination. Should these documents be admitted into evidence -- of course, they were referred to. The witness has testified about them. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. I -- I do seek their admission. And additionally, there were a number of other reports that we were waiting for MFI numbers to be given to. These specific reports -- and I'll deal with those first because the witness did identify each -- each one of those and identified material in each one of those, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The concern of the Chamber is - and that might be considered when deciding the matter - is that it might be appropriate rather to leave it at the witness comments on these reports in her testimony, rather than to bring in a lot of other material which might be not relevant, might -- we have, of course, not looked at all these documents in its entirety. And to admit it into evidence could give us great surprises at a later stage. For that reason, the Chamber would certainly urge the Defence to reconsider that position and to see whether we could not satisfy ourselves with what the witness said and what was put to her in relation to these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: To -- to the extent these -- these are records of -- truly contemporaneous records of daily reporting, I think they are of assistance to the Chamber. However, I take the Chamber's words in mind --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- and will come back to the Chamber with regard to this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we move on to P1212, which is a report by Human Rights Watch. The Chamber would invite you, Mr. Re, to specify which parts of the report you would seek to have admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I can imagine that you could not give an answer immediately, but perhaps you could inform the Chamber as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I can do that fairly quickly, but I just wouldn't be able to do it on my feet --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- while we're standing here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apart from that, it's 13 minutes to 2.00. So for that reason -- when do you think you could specify the portions of the report?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I can have that by tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: By tomorrow. Then we'll -- Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We can deal with that tomorrow. We oppose the admission of the report or any portion --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand that. But we are now, I think, in a bit of a different situation where the Chamber has invited the Prosecution to ... Then we have D205, which was tendered from the bar table. Either we can decide on admission, then it should be admitted under seal, because there are some data on D205 which, I would say, for names, layout of certain matters, which are not for the public. So we could admit it under seal. There is another possibility that the parties would agree on what is the basic content of D205; that is, that upon measurement, this document tells us that Mr. Balaj measures 1 metre, 78 centimetres. If the parties could agree on that, we don't need the document any more. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I would hope so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, you'd agree to that? Then we can ...

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we vacate D205.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I might, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'd like to raise very quickly. This deals with Witness 28.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And specifically, this arises in another matter. I was reviewing her 92 ter statement. And I feel that incumbent upon myself to object to paragraph 73 of her statement inasmuch as it contains information with regard to a witness who had previously testified in these proceedings for whom the Prosecution never led any of that evidence. And I'll leave it at that at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's on the record. We'll -- you will imagine that I couldn't give an immediate answer to that. Then I'd like to -- I think we have to ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There is one more matter, one more decision; that is, in relation to witness Gojkovic, numbers P1194 up to and including P1203. With an exception of two, they're admitted into evidence. Not yet admitted into evidence is annex 8, which is P1199. The same document is tendered through Witness 69 as well. A final decision will be taken in relation to this document once we have dealt thoroughly with Witness 69 as well. So therefore, that one is still pending. Then in relation to P1202 ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber has decided in relation to P1202 to take more time to consider whether it should admit that document or not. The others - that means P1194 up to and including P1198, then P1200 and 1201 and P1203 - are admitted into evidence. Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can I just correct myself. As Your Honour rightly pointed out, I think in relation to Exhibit P -- or former MFI P1192, where I said, "The value is that it's the witness's contemporaneous account of what happened to his relative when he went to identify his relative -- went to identify his relative. The words are audible. There's a transcript." When I said that, I was relying upon my memory. I correct myself. It wasn't the witness's contemporaneous account of what happened to his relative. It was actually the witness's contemporaneous account of what happened to him, where he said that he was taken from the KLA. It's my faulting memory. That was the -- that was the purpose for which we were attempting to -- to tender into evidence that transcript. But it's already part of Exhibit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll consider this, Mr. Re, whether this is sufficient good cause shown to reconsider our decision in relation to that video. I would like to thank very much interpreters, technicians, and court reporters, but also security - we often forget about security - for their indulgence and their patience this morning, which was a very fruitful housekeeping session. We adjourn until Monday ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Monday, quarter past 2.00, Courtroom I.
